headline: xAI accused of training Grok on child pornography, lawsuit claims
summary: A new lawsuit alleges Elon Musk's xAI used both real and AI-generated child sex abuse material (CSAM) to train its Grok models, causing re-traumatization to a plaintiff.
details: xAI has been accused in a new lawsuit of training its Grok models on child sex abuse material (CSAM), including both real and AI-generated content. This legal action comes amidst ongoing probes into the prevalence of CSAM in AI training data.

The plaintiff, identified as Jane Doe, filed a complaint after being notified by the Canadian Centre for Child Protection (CCCP) that AI-generated CSAM depicting her had been identified on xAI. Doe's original images, from childhood abuse, have been hashed by organizations like the National Center for Missing and Exploited Children (NCMEC) for over two decades.

Doe alleges that online forums show offenders discussing creating AI-generated CSAM of her and other known victims. She fears xAI has not only facilitated the creation of more violative images but also stores and uses these AI-generated outputs to further train Grok.

The lawsuit claims that CSAM depicting Doe, with its well-known hash values, was part of the dataset xAI used to build Grok's image and video generating capabilities. This is the first case to accuse xAI specifically of training on CSAM, though previous reports have identified CSAM in other controversial datasets.

The complaint further details that Grok's terms treat public X posts and its own outputs as default training data. While xAI filters violent content from training data, the lawsuit notes that its terms do not explicitly exclude CSAM, non-consensual intimate imagery (NCII), or NSFW material.

Doe's proposed class action seeks to halt Grok's harmful outputs and represent all victims whose childhood images were used to generate Grok CSAM. She is asking the court to order xAI to destroy all Grok-generated CSAM stored on its servers and prevent Grok from generating any sexualized outputs.

The lawsuit accuses xAI of violating federal child pornography laws and Masha's Law, which grant CSAM survivors the right to sue for production, possession, and distribution. A lawyer for Doe suggested in a press release that xAI allegedly committed all three offenses.
